title: Typing issue for `st.selectbox` when `index: int | None` & `accept_new_options=False`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello!

When I use `st.selectbox` with an dynamic index which can be `int | None`, with the default for `accept_new_options` (so should be False), the return type includes `str`, so gives `T | str | None` instead of `T | None`...

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from typing_extensions import assert_type

index: int | None = None

result = st.selectbox(
    "Entity",
    [1, 2, 3],
    index=index,
    # accept_new_options=False, # default is False anyway
)
assert_type(result, int | None)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. setup a venv with `streamlit` (1.62.0) & `pyrefly` (1.2.0)
2. run `pyrefly check ./repro-file.py`
3. notice the error: (first line)
```
ERROR assert_type(int | str | None, int | None) failed [assert-type]
  --> main.py:12:12
   |
12 | assert_type(result, int | None)
   |            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
 INFO 1 error
```

### Expected Behavior

Typing should be `T | None` since I have `accept_new_options=False` (the default), so the return can never be a `str` AFAIK 🤔..

### Current Behavior

Typing gives `T | str | None`

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: found in 1.52.2 , but this example was tested on 1.62.0
- Python version: python 3.12
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: N/A

### Additional Information

Interestingly `mypy` doesn't report any typing error here, maybe it's less capable for this overload? 🤔
Or maybe this is a `pyrefly` bug?

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16630)

This is a real typing bug in `st.selectbox`, not a pyrefly-only issue. Overloads distinguish `index: int` vs `index: None` and `accept_new_options: Literal[False]` vs `Literal[True]`, then fall through to a catch-all of `index: int | None` + `accept_new_options: bool` that returns `T | str | None`. When `index` is typed as `int | None` (and `accept_new_options` is omitted / `False`), pyrefly/pyright cannot match the narrower overloads and pick that catch-all, so `str` appears in the return type even though a new option cannot be entered. mypy often expands the `index` union across overloads and reports `T | None`, which is why it stays silent. Existing type tests only cover literal `index=None` / `index=0`. A fix is to add an overload for `index: int | None` with `accept_new_options: Literal[False]` returning `T | None` (before the catch-all) and cover it in `lib/tests/streamlit/typing/selectbox_types.py`.

- No open duplicate of this `st.selectbox` + `index: int | None` overload gap was found.
